body:
Maria C: Heads-up team — we have a scheduled control-plane edge-router firmware update in us-west1 on 2026-03-24 02:00–02:30 UTC. This is a small kernel/firmware patch to the border routers that carry inference ingress. No model or API changes involved.

Alex R: Thanks — expected customer impact? Any risk of dropped requests or sustained latency?

Maria C: Short version: possible very short connection resets during brief BGP flaps while each router applies the firmware (we expect 0–30s per router during the switch). Most clients will reconnect gracefully. We’ll keep warm spares and stagger the rollout to avoid simultaneous flaps across PoPs. For Dedicated customers with pinned egress, our routing policy will attempt failover to the configured secondary region — if their policies block egress, they may see transient failures.

Samir: Can we do a staged rollout (per rack/pop) rather than all border routers at once?

Maria C: Yes — plan is staggered by PoP: patch pop-a pair, wait 15m for telemetry, then proceed to next PoP. Ops doc has the exact PoP ordering (us-west1-pop-a -> pop-b -> pop-c).

Jade (oncall): I’ll be the primary oncall for the window, Alex is +1. I’ll be reachable on pager and will open an incident channel in #eng-oncall when we go live.

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: MNT-1732109876-ROUTER-PATCH assigned to Jade. Priority: P2 (scheduled maintenance).

Maria C: Draft status page blurb (please review):

statuspage-bot: Draft queued for review.

Maria C: "We will perform scheduled network firmware maintenance in the us-west1 region on 2026-03-24 02:00–02:30 UTC. During the maintenance we may observe brief connection resets or transient latency for inference traffic. Most clients will automatically reconnect; no action is required for typical workloads. Dedicated customers with strict egress policies may experience short failover to a secondary region. Estimated impact: under 1 minute for the majority of requests; isolated flows may see interruptions up to 30 seconds. No data loss expected."

Alex R: Wording looks good — please add a link to the status page contact and the support email for enterprise customers. Also add a pointer to the client retry best-practices doc.

Maria C: Updated snippet: 

"For questions during the window, visit https://status.redwood.ai or email support@redwood.ai (Enterprise customers: please cc your account team). See https://docs.redwood.ai/clients/retries for retry guidance."

Jade (oncall): Plan for comms:
- 01:50 UTC: post statuspage as "Maintenance starting soon"
- 02:00 UTC: update statuspage to show "In progress" and open #eng-oncall incident thread
- 02:30 UTC: target completion, then update statuspage to "Completed"
I’ll also send the 10-minute PAGER banner to the oncall group.

Samir: Ops checklist (short form):
- confirm coordinator container and healthchecks are green
- mark router pair as maintenance in inventory: `opsctl maintenance add router-rack-<X>`
- apply firmware to router-A, wait 30s, rotate traffic to router-B
- monitor 1-min p95 latency and socket-reset counters
- if >5% 5xx or >60s sustained errors, rollback patch on that pair
- remove maintenance flag: `opsctl maintenance remove router-rack-<X>`

Maria C: Rollback and patch commands to copy into runbook: 

```
opsctl patch router --id router-A --firmware v2.0.3
opsctl rotate-traffic --from router-A --to router-B --grace 30s
opsctl patch router --id router-B --firmware v2.0.3
```

Jade (oncall): Got it. I’ll keep live notes in #eng-oncall and post a single-line summary to #announcements when the maintenance completes.

Maria C: Customer email template (internal draft) — will send to Dedicated customer list T-24h, pls review: 

```
Subject: Scheduled maintenance: Network firmware update (us-west1) — 2026-03-24

Hi <CustomerName>,

We are scheduling a short network firmware update in our us-west1 region on 2026-03-24 from 02:00–02:30 UTC. During the update you may observe brief reconnections or short transient latency. Most traffic reconnects automatically and no action is required. If you run traffic that is sensitive to transient disconnects, reply and we can advise failover options or coordinate a different window.

For support during the window, visit https://status.redwood.ai or email support@redwood.ai (Enterprise customers: please cc your account team).

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Ops
```

Alex R: Nit — add the client retry best-practices link to the email (see docs link above).

Maria C: Added. Final customer message goes out T-24h. I’ll also add a KB note about client reconnect behavior.

Jade (oncall): Quick live mitigation runbook to paste into #eng-oncall when we go live:
1) If we see >1% 5xx across routes, trigger immediate rollback for the current pair and open a bridge.
2) If p95 latency doubles for >5 min, throttle background/non-critical jobs (eval/ingest), enable cache-prefetching, and escalate to SRE.
3) If a Dedicated customer reports sustained errors, follow their DR: failover to secondary region per their config and open an SR with SRE.

Samir: After patching, remember to rebalance routing weights (we have a helper script):

```
ssh ops@router-control
./scripts/reweight-pop --region us-west1 --to 0.98
```

pagerduty-bot: Reminder scheduled: 10 minutes until maintenance (to: #eng-oncall).

Maria C: Timeline recap: 
- 01:45 UTC: final go/no-go check
- 01:50 UTC: statuspage "Maintenance starting soon"
- 02:00 UTC: begin staged patching (per PoP)
- 02:30 UTC: target finish
- 02:35 UTC: statuspage "Maintenance completed"

Jade (oncall): I’ll hand off to Alex if anything spills past the window. If no escalation, I plan to close the PD incident by 03:00 UTC. @Alex R — standby as +1.

Alex R: Ack, standby.

statuspage-bot: Status page event published: maintenance ID mnt-2026-03-24-usw1 — https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/mnt-2026-03-24-usw1

Maria C: Thanks all. I’ll post the T-24h customer email in this thread for a last quick sign-off. If anything changes prior to T-2h, update this thread. :thumbsup:

Jade (oncall): Signed off from my side."
